recent_articles.title: KABIL acquires five critical mineral blocks in Argentina - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL)**, a joint venture of **National Aluminium Company Ltd. (NALCO)** and **Hindustan Copper Ltd. (HCL)**, has secured five critical mineral blocks in Argentina, marking a significant step towards reducing India's heavy reliance on imports.  Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy announced the acquisition during a press conference in Hyderabad, emphasizing the importance of securing overseas mineral assets to bolster domestic capabilities and achieve long-term self-reliance. The **National Critical Minerals Mission**, with an outlay of ₹32,000 crore, aims to strengthen domestic capabilities and achieve long-term self-reliance by addressing India's current dependence on imports for nearly 93% of its critical mineral requirements.

recent_articles.title: CM seeks cooperation of parties cutting across political lines in the development of the city - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** urged the **BJP** and **BRS** to cooperate in developing the state capital as a global city, urging them to put aside political differences for the benefit of the people.  He criticized **Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy**, accusing him of "hobnobbing" with **BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao** and hindering project approvals from the central government.

recent_articles.title: Kishan Reddy slams CM Revanth Reddy, says State running on Central funds - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Kishan Reddy**, Union Minister for Coal & Mines, refuted **A. Revanth Reddy's** accusations against the Modi government, stating that the Congress government relies on funds and support from the central government to sustain its administration. He highlighted the lack of implementation of poll promises, including the promised ₹500 bonus for paddy growers and financial assistance for agricultural laborers, as evidence of the government's failure.

recent_articles.title: Chamala counters Kishan Reddy, seeks clarity on Centre’s support - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bhuvanagiri MP Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy** criticized **Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy**, demanding clarification on his stance on Telangana issues and questioning his commitment to the state's development.  **Kiran Kumar Reddy** also challenged **Kishan Reddy's** claims of being a champion for Telangana, urging him to focus on fulfilling the people's expectations given his past electoral success in the state.

recent_articles.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy accuses his Maharashtra counterpart of showing callous apathy towards Tummidihatti barrage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** accused **Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis** of being apathetic to his requests for talks regarding the construction of the proposed Tummidihatti barrage in Telangana's Adilabad district.  **Revanth Reddy** demanded that **Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy** take the initiative to facilitate these talks, warning that farmers would erupt in anger if the project is not completed. He also asserted that the state government was committed to purchasing all procured paddy and maize by June 15th or face consequences, including dumping the grains in front of BJP leaders' houses.

recent_articles.title: BJP targets DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over Sanatana Dharma remarks - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** condemned **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, a DMK leader, for his remarks on Sanatana Dharma in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.  **G. Kishan Reddy**, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, accused the DMK of "poisonous politics" and "anti-Hindu rhetoric." The BJP also criticized the Congress party's support for Stalin's comments and questioned **Vijay**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on his silence regarding the issue.

recent_articles.title: Modi to set the tone for capturing Telangana after Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** is scheduled to visit Telangana on Sunday, marking a significant push by the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** to establish itself as a major electoral force in the state.  Party leaders believe the Prime Minister's address will signal the BJP's intention to capture power in the next Assembly elections and are confident that his popularity will help expand their base.  **N. Ramchander Rao**, **Union Ministers G. Kishan Reddy** and **Bandi Sanjay Kumar** and party workers are anticipating a strong response from the public.

recent_articles.title: BJP women cadre accuse Congress of blocking quota bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Telangana BJP** organized a women's protest march on Thursday evening, criticizing the **Congress party** for its perceived "hypocritical and anti-women stance" on women's reservation in legislatures. The march, which began at Domalguda and culminated in a public meeting at Indira Park, saw thousands of women party workers and supporters participate, with senior leaders like **N. Ramchander Rao**, **G. Kishan Reddy**, **Bandi Sanjay Kumar**, **K. Laxman**, **D.K. Aruna**, **Eatala Rajender**, **Yeleti Maheswar Reddy**, and **Malka Komuraiah** taking part.

recent_articles.title: Centre ensuring fuel security despite global turmoil, says Ramchander Rao - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Ramchander Rao**, BJP Telangana president, expressed confidence in the Modi government's handling of global challenges and assured the public that there is no shortage of domestic LPG. **Rao** stated that while gas prices have risen globally by 20% to 50%, India has maintained stable fuel prices due to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "astute diplomatic" leadership.  He highlighted the arrival of large LPG vessels carrying 92,700 metric tonnes and assured the public there is no cause for concern. **G. Kishan Reddy**, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, also extended Ugadi greetings, emphasizing that the term "Parabhava" does not apply to India or its people but is meant for enemies and anti-national forces.

recent_articles.title: Centre to upgrade 5,008 ‘Anganwadi’ centres in Telangana at ₹30.04 crore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
**G. Kishan Reddy**, **Union Minister for Coal and Mines**, announced that the **Centre** will upgrade 5,008 **Anganwadi Centres (AWCs)** in Telangana at a cost of ₹30.04 crore as ‘Saksham Anganwadis’. This initiative is part of the ‘Mission Saksham Anganwadi’ and ‘Poshan 2.0’ scheme, which aims to strengthen nearly two lakh **Anganwadi** centres across the country by improving nutrition and early childhood care and education.  The upgraded centres will be equipped with enhanced infrastructure, including LED screens, water filtration systems, 'Poshan Vatika' (nutrition gardens), early childhood education material, and Building as Learning Aid (BaLA) paintings. 

**Mr. Reddy** highlighted the importance of the **Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP)** in bridging the gap between the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) and Average Daily Intake (ADI). He stated that fortified rice is being supplied to **Anganwadi centres** to meet micronutrient requirements and control anaemia among women and children.  The focus on millets, at least once a week in meal preparation, is also emphasized. The upgraded centres will be located across various districts in Telangana.
